step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates Ticketmaster's multi-region checkout system. User traffic enters via a CDN (CloudFront) configured for latency/geo-routing across active-active regions. Page rendering requests go to Next.js hosted on Amazon EKS. API requests are centralized in AWS AppSync using GraphQL. For simple single-step queries/operations, AppSync triggers AWS Lambda, which interacts with Amazon DynamoDB. For multi-step purchase workflows (payment collection, order processing), AppSync triggers AWS Step Functions. For long-running mutations, AppSync returns asynchronous responses to the client via WebSocket subscriptions. DynamoDB Global Tables replicate data bidirectionally across regions. All components map directly to the valid vocabulary list. Flows are organized logically into page rendering, single-step operations, multi-step purchase processes, and cross-region replication.

edges.notes: User accesses checkout web application via CDN.
CDN routes web page rendering requests to Next.js on EKS.
AppSync triggers Lambda for single-step queries and data retrieval.
Lambda retrieves and stores session and event data in DynamoDB.
AppSync triggers Step Functions for multi-step purchase workflows.
AppSync pushes real-time asynchronous updates back to CDN/client using WebSocket subscriptions.
DynamoDB Global Tables perform bidirectional active-active data replication across regions.
